entities.summary: Manu Chao is a French-Spanish musician. He sings in French, Spanish, English, Italian, Arabic, Catalan, Galician, Portuguese, Greek, and occasionally in other languages. Chao began his musical career in Paris, busking and playing with groups such as Hot Pants and Los Carayos, which combined a variety of languages and musical styles. With friends and his brother Antoine Chao, he founded the band Mano Negra in 1987, achieving considerable success, particularly in Europe. He became a solo artist after its breakup in 1995 and since then has toured regularly with his live band, Radio Bemba Sound System.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Manu Chao's music played a significant role in popularizing Latin American and global musical styles in Europe during the late 20th century. His band Mano Negra achieved considerable success in Europe, particularly among young people, contributing to the growth of alternative rock and world music.
